gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the BLUETTI AC180, ChatGPT's 'best overall' pick, has an ECO mode that switches the AC outlet off after the load stays at or below a 15–30 W threshold for 1, 2, 3 or 4 hours. A blanket on low, or one whose thermostat has cycled off, can lose power partway through the night unless ECO is turned off.
standout_why: I opened four rival pages. WattFort (cited) covers Sunbeam's 'do not use with generators, power converters or inverters' and KickAss's 45/90/120-minute 12 V timers, but says nothing about a power station's own low-load auto-off. BlackoutWise (cited) has no compatibility statements: no ECO or auto-off, no car-port limit and no waveform. RuntimeMath only notes Pure Enrichment's 10-hour blanket auto-off. Tested Watts only gives a car-outlet limit of about 120–126 W. None of them mentions ECO mode, energy-saving mode or a low-load AC cut-off on any station, so this setting is the new fact.
decides: It does not change the pick. The AC180 still fits a 120 V blanket overnight. It adds a required setup step: turn ECO off, or set it to the lowest threshold and longest duration, before a night on low. Otherwise a low-draw blanket can lose power within 1–4 hours. Jackery and Anker have similar energy-saving features, but I could not read their thresholds from the makers' documents, so the page should not claim this is AC180-only or say the other stations are exempt.

findings.label: ECO mode low-load AC auto-off
findings.value: AC output turns off when load is at or below a user-set 15–30 W (DC: 5–10 W) for 1, 2, 3 or 4 h; ECO can be switched on or off on the screen
findings.source_title: BLUETTI AC180 user manual, 5. Appendix, 5.1 FAQs Q4 (ManualsLib copy, English section, p. 18)
findings.note: Manual text: 'When operating on ECO mode, the AC/DC output will automatically turn off if the AC180 is bearing low or no load for a while. You can set the power threshold of AC output and DC output to 15-30W /5-10W, respectively, for 1, 2, 3, or 4 hours.' This is a third-party copy of BLUETTI's manual. BLUETTI's own US page and PDF could not be read from here. The manual does not give the default ECO state, and it does not say whether a blanket whose thermostat cycles above and below the threshold resets the timer.

findings.label: Blanket-side auto-off cap (Pure Enrichment)
findings.value: Pure Enrichment heated blankets switch off after 10 h
findings.source_title: How Long Will a Power Station Run an Electric Blanket? 18 Models (RuntimeMath)
findings.note: RuntimeMath cites Pure Enrichment for the PureRelief Deluxe Heated Blanket. I did not open Pure Enrichment's own manual. This is the blanket's own timer, separate from the power station's ECO cut-off: a full 10 h night uses that timer up.

findings.label: Blanket maker that bans inverter use (already on a cited rival)
findings.value: Sunbeam heated bedding manual: do not use 'with generators, power converters or inverters'; use only on a 110–120 V, 60 Hz AC circuit; no extension cord
findings.source_title: How Long Will a Power Station Run an Electric Blanket? | WattFort
findings.note: WattFort, cited by ChatGPT, already states this, so it is not new for our page. I did not open the Sunbeam manual myself; the wording above is as WattFort reports it. WattFort also reports that Sunbeam's auto-off timer resets after a power cut, so the blanket stays off until someone presses its power button, which matters if the station's ECO cuts power.
